hero.noResults: We couldn't find an entry for this term.

common.note: [PLACEHOLDER] General notice or disclaimer at the end of the page. Industry-specific legal text must be approved by the company.

complete.title: You have reviewed all {{total}} criteria
complete.text: [PLACEHOLDER] Short text that guides the reader to the next step once the list is complete. It invites them to seek expert advice or get in touch without promising a definite result.

intro.title: How does the knowledge center work?
intro.lead: This page is not meant to be read from start to finish. It is a reference book you search and open. Each entry can be read on its own, with its own number and shareable address.
body: As soon as you start typing in the search box in the hero, the chapter rows are replaced by results. Search ignores case and accents.
The small emblem in this entry sits next to the large text, at the same height. On narrow screens it moves below the text.

overview.title: Entry layout
overview.lead: Each entry starts with a number, a title and a highlighted definition. Details continue with paragraphs, lists, tables or steps.
body: Wide images sit below the text at full width and enlarge when clicked. External links in the text are marked <docs>like this</docs> and open in a new tab.
overview.listIntro: A numbered list is for items where order matters:
list: The first item, its number is shown in the accent colour.
The second item, rows are separated by a thin line.
The third item, long text continues from the start of the line.

scope.title: Flow list
scope.lead: Long lists of equally weighted items are not shown item by item, but as a single block of text separated by slashes.

principle.title: Highlighted statement
principle.lead: A short answer to the question can be added to the start of the large text with a highlighted label.
principle.callout: The sentence highlighted like a marker pen is the one idea the reader should remember from the entry.
outro: Paragraphs after the highlight complete the entry. Using at most one highlight per entry is recommended.

guideIntro.title: Image in the side column
guideIntro.lead: On wide screens, this entry's image does not sit next to the text but below the entry index on the left, filling the remaining space in the column.
body: The image is only visible while its own entry is being read. When the reader moves on to another entry, it fades out.
On phones and portrait tablets there is no side column, so the image stays next to or below the text.
To get this behaviour, add imageInAside: true to the entry definition. If a chapter has two entries with images, leaving at least one entry between them keeps the first image on screen long enough.

comparison.title: Comparison table
comparison.lead: The table turns into cards on narrow screens. Row names can link to the related entry.

rows.use: [PLACEHOLDER] Short description of when the first option fits.
[PLACEHOLDER] Short description of when the second option fits.

optionA.title: What is option A?
optionA.lead: This entry also shows its image in the side column. Document images are not fitted to the screen when enlarged; they open at full size and scroll.

optionB.title: What is option B?
optionB.lead: An entry without an image. It shows an unnumbered list and a closing sentence.
optionB.more: The closing sentence in bold guides the reader to the next step.

criteria.title: Check before you decide
criteria.lead: The accent-coloured chapter is the page's moment of decision. The list can be ticked, progress shows in the counter in the left column, and once everything is ticked a dialog opens that leads to the contact page.

process.title: Process steps
process.lead: Steps that are only read, not ticked, are shown as numbered rows.

closing.title: The right decision starts with the right information.
closing.lead: [PLACEHOLDER] Description of the short, large sentence that closes the chapter.

faqStart.title: Where should I start?
faqStart.lead: [PLACEHOLDER] Short answer to the frequently asked question. Readers go to the related entry for details through the "See" link.

faqHelp.lead: [PLACEHOLDER] Short answer guiding the reader to the checklist or the contact page.
